chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever reaches al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained hajj (pilgrimage).

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: reached or attained within the required time
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, used here to mark the legal time boundary
key_terms.الْحَجَّ: hajj (pilgrimage), the major pilgrimage to the sacred sites
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ: al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, the sacred site of standing during hajj
key_terms.تَزُولَ: to pass the zenith; to decline from midday

ai.seo_question: By what time must a pilgrim reach al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām for their hajj to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for attaining hajj by reaching al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām before the sun passes its zenith. It highlights the importance of the prescribed time limits within the rites of hajj and indicates that reaching this point within that time is sufficient for the pilgrimage to be counted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2775 - Abdullah ibn al-Mughira narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said: "
Whoever reaches al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument) before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained Hajj."
